commentary: With market breadth scored at a defensive 36% under deterministic WEAK conditions, Stan Weinstein's stage discipline and William O'Neil's market-direction rules mandate rigorous defensive posture. While key benchmark indices attempt relief bounces above major psychological marks, institutional distribution remains an overhead threat. In accordance with O'Neil's CANSLIM criteria, true leadership requires confirmed quarterly earnings acceleration (C+A) alongside high-volume breakouts, rather than speculative unconfirmed turns. Mark Minervini's SEPA principles dictate keeping exposure progressive, restricting fresh capital exclusively to authenticated Stage 2 leaders displaying volume-backed base breakouts, and executing pre-planned stop losses immediately upon any technical failure.
